title: Full project review: tests C+, docs C+, data not fit for training
detail: Principal review of the whole repository. Tests graded C+ (many passed without executing solvers, data checks mixed into the unit run, the audit ledger polluted by test runs). Documentation graded C+ (stale commands, retired Markdown layer still described, mixed-language skills). Data judged NOT fit for training: grounded-paraphrase injected unstated negative premises into about 64% of the training mix; about 70% of the mix came from one templated corpus; targets were predictable from the CONTEXT block instead of the message. Consequence: no current corpus qualifies, and training stays prohibited regardless (AGENTS.md rule 3).

title: Test suite hardened: 508 tests passing, solvers actually executed
detail: npm test passed 508 tests. Solver-backed tests now execute the native solvers instead of skipping silently; long data tests moved to a separate npm run test:data; tests no longer append verdicts to the real audit ledger (CHATSOP_AUDIT_LEDGER points at a temporary directory); fixed the HTTP reinforcement trace bug (the chat trace now reports reinforcement from the executed packet).

title: Documentation fixes: audit command, retired Markdown layer, English skills, glossary
detail: Corrected the corpus-audit command (node tools/datasets/audit-corpus.mjs --corpus <name>), removed descriptions of the retired Markdown dataset layer (JSONL-first since 2026-09-28), translated the remaining skills to English, extended the wiki glossary and fixed the acronym: SOP = Standard Operating Procedure; the language is SOP Lang.

title: Corpus-audit checker: faithfulness, triviality, diversity, template leakage
detail: tools/datasets/audit-corpus.mjs audits every corpus and fails closed: entity and polarity faithfulness of each grounded/problem wire against the message, triviality, template diversity (distinct masked templates, top-template share) and template-level leakage between train/dev and the sealed test (exact input, masked template, near duplicate, target skeleton, entity heads). Results are in eval/reports/current/corpus-audit/<corpus>.json; most legacy corpora fail faithfulness or leakage checks, which confirms the review verdict.

title: Phase 0 and phase 1 wire fixes
detail: Every wire help page example is now executed by tests/wire-help.test.mjs, so documentation cannot drift from the parser. Runtime conformance for fact source assumption: a fact carrying source assumption is handled as an assumption, not as sourced evidence.

title: Owner decision: stated / assumed / unclear wires, one keyword per line
detail: The small model reports what the message says with stated, what it adds with assumed, and an unintelligible or request-free message with unclear. One keyword per line.

title: Owner decision: no model context; string-based targets with the closed role set
detail: The formalizer input is the user message only (no shortlist, identifiers, knowledge or clock). Targets are quoted strings: a relation phrase plus roles from the closed set subject, object, recipient, location, source, destination, instrument, time, topic. The host links strings to the lexicon.

title: Owner decision: unclear = gibberish | no_request
detail: unclear has exactly two kinds: gibberish (unintelligible) and no_request (no statement and no question). Nothing else is unclear.

title: Owner decision: no model-level refusal
detail: The model never refuses; every message is formalized. What the reasoner can conclude is decided by the host, not by the model.

title: Owner decision: allowJsEval removed
detail: The allowJsEval policy switch is removed; JavaScript evaluation stays a trusted, coding-agent capability and is never a small-model target.

title: Owner decision: English by default, Romanian on request
detail: Answers are in English unless the request or the message asks for Romanian.

title: Owner decision: sources de-quarantined as inspiration only
detail: QQP, PAWS, ProofWriter, AmbigNQ, QA2D and SQuAD may be used as inspiration for structure, phenomena and statistics, never copied text; tools/datasets/no-copy.mjs proves no row is copied.

title: Owner decision: real diversity required
detail: Corpora must show real linguistic and structural diversity, measured by the diversity auditor; templated variety does not count.

The corpus audit became a three-pane browser (category tree, paginated list, detail). The vocabulary check links every SOP wire type and field to its help page and flags undocumented ones; it found 0 hallucinations.

Most important: the training projection still sends a CONTEXT block, which must be fixed before any sop-agent-4 data is prepared for training.

title: Current work: data — what is being done now and why
detail: WHY: the review found the existing corpora unfit (unstated negatives injected in ~64% of the mix, ~70% from one templated corpus, targets predictable from CONTEXT), and sop-agent-4 removes the model context altogether, so every existing corpus (sop-agent-3 targets with a CONTEXT shortlist) must be rebuilt rather than patched. WHAT: (1) mine a diversity inventory of question types, paraphrase operations, ambiguity types and reasoning depth from the cached sources, taking structure and statistics only, never text; (2) generate cases from an intermediate representation and print them as sop-agent-4 string targets, with the message as the only model input and the world, ontology and expected result kept as evaluation-only scaffolding; (3) verify every target by executing it against its world; (4) enforce quotas and split grouping so the sealed test is not answerable by template recall; (5) audit the pilot for faithfulness, diversity and leakage; (6) only then regenerate all corpora. NOT DONE: no training, no fine-tuning; data qualification is a separate gate from the owner approval required by AGENTS.md rule 3.
